proof-narrative-lean-equiv.notes: The .md Theorem claims the eigenspace ratio is INVARIANT under continuous deformation q→q' up to a conformal factor; the Lean proves only that α cancels in (α·λ^n)/(α·λ^m). The baseline q' (q_baseline) never enters the conclusion, and λ being an eigenvalue is irrelevant — the Lean is a trivially-true cancellation strictly weaker than the stated invariance.

proof-statement-integrity.evidence: gauge-conformal-invariance.lean:26: "theorem gauge_conformal_invariance (q_local q_baseline : ℝ) (n m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hα : α > 0)"
proof-statement-integrity.notes: The Lean signature does not derive the .md claim: it concludes (α·λ^n)/(α·λ^m)=λ^n/λ^m, an α-cancellation true for ANY α≠0 and ANY λ, independent of the substrate deformation. The theorem name asserts 'gauge conformal invariance' but the goal is a content-free algebraic identity — a passing-by-weakening.

proof-no-self-assuming-projection.notes: Not a self-assuming projection; it is a (vacuous) algebraic cancellation, a different defect.

proof-no-trivial-true.notes: The goal is a tautology discharged by mul_div_mul_left for any α≠0, ignoring the substrate/eigenvalue content the statement is about; it is the 'true but content-free' pattern this criterion targets.

proof-no-false-premise.notes: Premise α>0 is fine and satisfiable; no False-elim.

proof-no-unused-hypotheses.notes: q_baseline is entirely unused; q_local enters only as λ=eigenvalue_plus q_local but its eigenvalue nature is irrelevant to the cancellation; n,m are arbitrary. The invariance-under-q→q' content (q_baseline) is never exercised.

proof-no-decide-masking.notes: No decide; the defect is vacuity/cancellation, not decide-masking.

da-false-claim.notes: The eigenvalue formula λ±=½[h±√(h²+4)] (char poly λ²−hλ−1) is correct; no false mathematical assertion (the issue is the Lean not proving the claim, recorded under da-vacuous).

da-vacuous.notes: The theorem backing this 'Theorem (Gauge conformal invariance)' is the content-free identity (α·x)/(α·y)=x/y; it proves nothing about eigenspace ratios being invariant under substrate deformation. Genuinely vacuous relative to its title/statement.

da-circular.notes: No circular derivation (there is essentially no derivation).

da-overclaim.evidence: gauge-conformal-invariance.md:2: "invariant under continuous deformations of the substrate q → q', up to a global conformal scaling factor α(q,q')"
da-overclaim.notes: A 'Theorem' of substrate-deformation invariance is asserted, but only an α-cancellation is proven; the conclusion is far stronger than the (vacuous) argument supports — conditional/structural claim presented as a proved theorem.

da-hidden-dof.notes: α is the disclosed conformal factor; not a hidden calibration.

da-non-sequitur.notes: From 'α cancels in a ratio of powers of one fixed λ' it does NOT follow that 'the eigenspace ratio is invariant under q→q''; the deformation q_local→q_baseline is never related. The theorem's conclusion does not follow from its (trivial) proof.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: Lean proves something strictly weaker/vacuous vs the .md claim of substrate-deformation invariance — the canonical proof-statement-integrity divergence.

da-citation-misuse.notes: No external citations in block or Lean.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: gauge-conformal-invariance.md:2: "the relative ratio of their eigenspaces is invariant ... up to a global conformal scaling factor α(q,q')"
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: 'relative ratio of eigenspaces', 'conformal scaling factor α(q,q')', and 'topological partitions corresponding to emission poles n and m' are never made precise enough to pin the intended claim; the Lean's interpretation (ratio of powers λ^n/λ^m of a single q-local eigenvalue) is one of several incompatible readings.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: No specific physical prediction to contradict measurement; the defect is formal vacuity.

da-reproducibility.notes: Lean compiles to a trivial identity; reproducible, just not the claimed result.

da-referee-verdict.notes: This 'Theorem' is backed by a vacuous Lean: gauge_conformal_invariance proves only (α·λ^n)/(α·λ^m)=λ^n/λ^m (mul_div_mul_left), with q_baseline unused and λ's eigenvalue nature irrelevant. The narrative claim — eigenspace ratios invariant under substrate deformation q→q' up to a conformal factor — is not established at all. Strongest objection: either prove genuine q→q' invariance (relating eigenvalue_plus q_local and q_baseline) or demote to a conjecture/remark; the current state is a passing-by-trivialisation.
